newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: EU to resume cooperation with new Congo - envoys.
newsitem.headline: EU to resume cooperation with new Congo - envoys.

text.p: The European Union said on Tuesday it was ready to resume economic cooperation with the former Zaire after five years of interruption.

An EU mission, wrapping up a two-day official visit to the renamed Democratic Republic of the Congo, told a news conference President Laurent Kabila appeared committed to respecting human rights and democracy.

Jacques Poos, deputy prime minister of Luxembourg and delegation leader, said: "This visit has been succesful. It will allow us to resume cooperation with the new authorities. It will be a partnership."
The four-member delegation held talks with Kabila and Foreign Minister Bizima Karaha.
Poos said there were indications that Kabila would go ahead with his declared plan to hold free and fair elections in the country in 1999. The EU would assist in organising the polls.

The EU severed links with Kinshasa in 1992, accusing former veteran dictator Mobutu Sese Seko of repeated human rights abuses and of not moving fast enough towards democracy. Mobutu fled the country just before Kabila's guerrilla forces swept into Kinshasa in mid-May, capping a seven-month armed campaign.
The EU has continued to channel financial assistance through non-governmental agencies, donating $400 million in the past five years for a wide range of programmes.
Poos could not say how much money the EU would make available to Democratic Congo for its reconstruction after years of mismanagement and neglect under Mobutu.
"We don't have precise figures yet," he said.
Poos cautioned against hasty judgment of Kabila, who granted himself sweeping powers and has banned political activity.

"The government intends to restore democracy within two years. It's a reasonable timing," he said. "Two months is not enough for us to judge the government on its willingness to stand by its programme."

The EU move follows the decision of former colonial power Belgium to resume full cooperation with Congo after six years. A German ministerial delegation was expected in Kinshasa later on Tuesday for aid talks.
